body:
**Root cause found + reliable workaround** (tested on macOS arm64, P2S profiles, Bambu Studio 02.x and current OrcaSlicer CLI — both crash identically, single filament too, so this isn't really about two filaments or support size):

The machine preset for P2S/X1-series carries a **dual-variant string for a single-extruder machine**:

```json
"extruder_variant_list": ["Direct Drive Standard,Direct Drive High Flow"]
"printer_extruder_variant": ["Direct Drive Standard,Direct Drive High Flow"]
```

One array element containing **two comma-separated variants** makes `DynamicPrintConfig::support_different_extruders()` return **true** (the variant set's size > 1), which pushes the CLI into the **multi-extruder slicing path** → SIGSEGV before any output. That's also why the GUI is unaffected for many users: the GUI resolves the variant differently than `--load-settings`.

Stock presets inherited/flattened for CLI use keep the dual-variant string, so any P2S/X1C flatten-and-slice workflow inherits the trigger. (Same area as #10083.)

**Workaround — collapse to one variant** in the machine config before slicing:

```json
"extruder_variant_list": ["Direct Drive Standard"],
"printer_extruder_variant": ["Direct Drive Standard"]
```

Also required for a clean CLI run with flattened presets (each tripped a different failure before the segfault):

- `"from": "system"` in every loaded profile (not `"user"`) plus matching `compatible_printers`, otherwise the process/printer compatibility check fails
- `"nozzle_volume_type": "Standard"` present (array or string — only a warning if absent)
- merge `machine_limits`/`cli_config.json` settings into the machine profile if you built it by hand

With the collapsed variant list, `--slice 0 --export-3mf` exits 0 and produces a valid plate on P2S. Working end-to-end invocation (OrcaSlicer CLI, but identical flags for BambuStudio):

```sh
OrcaSlicer --orient 1 --arrange 1 \
  --load-settings "process.json;machine.json" \
  --load-filaments "filament.json" \
  --slice 0 --export-3mf out.gcode.3mf model.stl
```

Worth checking whether the multi-extruder branch entered via a >1-size variant set is dereferencing per-extruder data that single-extruder presets never populate — that would explain the crash being data-dependent rather than filament-count-dependent.
